question: A SaaS vendor runs one Agent SDK deployment that serves many customer organizations from a single Anthropic credential. Support asks for a per-user, per-tenant audit trail of tool calls so they can answer 'which customer triggered this MCP action' during incident review. What should the engineering team implement?
options: A) Enable OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 so the full tool input and output bodies let an investigator infer, from their contents alone, which customer's data was involved
B) Provision and rotate a separate Anthropic API key for every customer organization so the credential used on each request identifies which tenant made that call
C) Have each customer stand up and operate their own self-hosted OpenTelemetry collector, then attempt to forward only their portion of the one shared telemetry stream to it
D) Inject percent-encoded enduser.id and tenant.id into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES per call so tool_decision, tool_result, and mcp_server_connection events carry the user and tenant
correct_answers: D) Inject percent-encoded enduser.id and tenant.id into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES per call so tool_decision, tool_result, and mcp_server_connection events carry the user and tenant
explanations: Tool content logging exposes payload bodies but does not attach an identifiable user or tenant attribute to the emitted events, so it does not solve the attribution requirement.
Per-customer keys would require restructuring authentication and billing for every tenant and still would not tag individual tool-call events with a user identity within a shared key's traffic.

The telemetry stream is not partitioned by tenant at the transport layer, so there is no mechanism to split a shared export stream per customer without the attribute tagging described in the correct option.

Correct. Attaching enduser.id and tenant.id as resource attributes on each call makes the security-relevant events (tool_decision, tool_result, mcp_server_connection, permission_mode_changed) attributable per end user, which is exactly the documented pattern for building a per-user audit trail from a shared credential.
